turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll type END MEETING on its own line, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have until 4:40, so I'll be brief. Owen found out about a zero from the gradebook on his phone, in the middle of class. Who decided that, and why didn't anyone call me first?
Thanks for coming in. The zero went in before I called you, and that was wrong.
Okay. On what basis did you enter it?
I will remove the zero tomorrow morning. Owen does a private supervised rewrite at lunch on Thursday. Nothing goes on his record. I will put all of that in an email to you tonight.
I'm writing that down. Does the zero come off tomorrow whatever happens Thursday, and does the email say "nothing goes on his record" in those words?
Yes, all of it, in writing tonight.
Okay. Owen will do the rewrite to put this behind him, and for no other reason. Copy the principal on that email, and I want it tonight.
Okay, I think that is the end of the meeting. Thank you.

Then we're agreed: the zero comes off tomorrow morning, Owen does a private supervised rewrite at lunch on Thursday, nothing goes on his record, and it's all in an email tonight with the principal copied. Anything else, Hale?
